result:
`bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` is 7 pass / 0 fail (the stack traces in the output are the app logging the expected 422/403 exceptions, as the pre-existing search test already did).

The vulnerability was in `PostController.update` (`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:88`), which fed the raw parsed request body straight into `Post.forceUpdate` — bypassing both the `PostPayloadSchema` validation the route already declares and the `Post.fillable` allowlist that deliberately omits `authorId`, so any client-sent `authorId`, `createdAt`, or empty `title` was written verbatim. I replaced that with `const data = await this.validateBody(PostPayloadSchema)` followed by `Post.update({ id: post.id }, data)`: the Zod object strips keys outside `title`/`excerpt`/`body` and enforces the same required/length rules as `store` (invalid input throws before any write, yielding a 422 with field errors), and `update` rather than `forceUpdate` keeps mass assignment bound to `Post.fillable` as a second line of defence — mirroring how `store` gets `authorId` from the session. Authorization still runs before validation, so non-authors get 403 as before. I also extended `tests/PostController.test.ts` with a `posts.update` feature suite covering the valid author edit, a body carrying another user's `authorId` (author unchanged), an out-of-form `createdAt` (ignored), an empty title (422, post untouched), and a non-author edit (403, post untouched).
